newsitem.title: CANADA: Hollinger takeover of Southam challenged.
newsitem.headline: Hollinger takeover of Southam challenged.

text.p: A non-profit group, the Council of Canadians, announced on Tuesday it has mounted a legal challenge to Hollinger Inc's takeover of the newspaper chain Southam Inc.
The challenge appeals against the federal Competition Bureau's approval of Hollinger's takeover of Southam earlier this year, the public-interest group said in a news release.

"The notice of motion presented to the Federal Court of Canada...argues the Competition Bureau erred in failing to consider the impact of the merger on Charter rights guaranteeing freedom of expression," it said.
The council said it would release details at a news conference at 1100 EDT/1500 GMT on Thursday.
Hollinger has gained effective control with 41 percent of Southam, and Hollinger's Conrad Black has taken over as Southam's chairman and chief executive officer.
Some Canadians have argued that an increasing concentration of newspaper ownership will reduce diversity of expression but the federal government has declined so far to intervene.
